title: CRS-22 Return
description: Scientists are excited to have their experiments back on Earth after research was done aboard the ISS. SpaceX's Dragon splashed down off the Florida coast July 9. A return near KSC means scientists can get their time-sensitive experiments quicker.
keywords: CRS, CRS-22, SpaceX, Cargo Dragon, Cargo Resupply, ISS, International Space Station, research, science experiments, splashdown, Kennedy Space Center, KSC, ambient blood samples, radishes
via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: So there's two of those. We got them both.
The astronauts go to space. They experience some immune system deficits.
And so we're trying to understand the mechanism of that and understand the breadth of that.
And so to do that, we get blood samples before and after space travel,
but that doesn't really tell us what's happening in the environment itself.
And so we've been able to negotiate the astronauts having to draw their blood samples while they're in space.
And so we also, another reason why it's important to get the blood quickly from space
is that to mitigate the effects of reentry so that the cells don't adapt to the Earth environment again.
If the goal is to go to deep space exploration, to go to the moon and then to Mars,
it's very important that we maintain the health of the astronauts.
So it's very important to understand what's going on and how to, if we can do anything to counter it.
So this is what I mean by processing the blood.
So we've layered the blood over a sucrose solution, which is a density solution.
And so most of the red blood cells all pile it into the bottom.
And this thin white band are the immune cells.
They separate away from the rest of the cells in the blood.
And this is what we're after. So right now I'm going to isolate that white band of cells.
And with that, I'm going to set up all the experiments.
